Short Line mortgages for $100, so any win \u2264$99 is +cash if I mortgage before I need rent survival. Bid $71 and keep raising $1 to $99; drop at $100+. Folding now gifts them ~$30 arb. $1 arb won't cover Boardwalk but drains them and pads Park Place survival. Never give States."}
message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to bid on SHORT_LINE in this auction.

I have $546 and p2 has $225. The current bid is $70. I previously planned to bid up to $99 and mortgage the property if I won. The mortgage value of a railroad is $100.

A $71 bid nets $29 cash after mortgaging. If p2 wins at $70, they would have $155 left and could mortgage for $100 to reach $255. The goal is to force them to pay more and drain their cash while keeping the option to mortgage if I win under $100.

p2 owns dangerous properties: Park Place and Boardwalk with three houses each, plus the full orange monopoly. I own light blue with four, three, and three houses respectively. States Avenue is unmortgaged but not part of a pink monopoly since p2 holds St. Charles and Virginia. Ventnor is unmortgaged.

No yellow monopoly exists for me since p2 mortgaged Atlantic and Marvin Gardens. The green monopoly is split and mostly mortgaged. I am now deciding whether to bid $71 or drop out.

Oriental Avenue with four houses pays $400. Vermont Avenue with three houses pays $270. Connecticut Avenue with three houses pays $300. These are substantial rent amounts.

p2's orange monopoly with four houses each pays $750, $750, and $800. That totals $2300 in combined rent. Park Place with three houses pays $1100. Boardwalk with three houses pays $1400. Landing on these properties would drain my entire cash balance.

I can mortgage States Avenue for $70 and Ventnor for $130. Selling the ten houses on my light blue properties would net $250. That combined with my $546 cash gives me roughly $896 in liquid assets.

The total liquid assets are roughly $1156. Boardwalk with three houses pays $1400, which exceeds this amount, so landing there would still bankrupt me even fully liquidated. Park Place at $1100 is survivable but would leave me nearly broke. If p2 wins the auction at $70, they would have $155 remaining.

If p2 wins at $70 and mortgages Short Line for $100, they end up with $255 and a net gain of $30. That is bad for me because the mortgage prevents rent collection until unmortgaged.

Bidding $71 instead would let me buy under $100 and mortgage for $100, netting $29 cash. If p2 drops out, I avoid paying the full $70 bid entirely.

Continuing to bid higher shrinks their arbitrage margin. The strategy of raising bids toward $99 remains sound.

Bidding above $100 is unwise because unmortgaging would cost $110. Winning at $71 leaves me with $575 after mortgaging, while winning at $99 leaves only $547. I am now weighing whether to drop out at $70 so p2 pays the full bid and keeps the property unmortgaged.

A single unmortgaged railroad pays only $25 in rent. p2 could unmortgage B&O later if needed.

With $155 cash remaining, they may struggle to pay my rents. I am checking which of my properties charge rent while they are on SHORT_LINE. Water Works is mortgaged and unrentable. The light blue properties with houses are all unrentable because I own no pink monopoly. States Avenue and Ventnor are also unrentable without a pink monopoly.

Draining p2's cash makes them more vulnerable to bankruptcy on my properties. Even with $155 remaining, they cannot pay $400 in rent without liquidating assets. Selling houses on Park Place and Boardwalk would generate cash, but that would also reduce their ability to pay my light blue rents.

Dark blue houses sell for $100 each, so p2 could liquidate $600 in assets if needed. The incremental bid strategy remains sound. I will not jump to a higher bid because the prior pattern shows p2 matches every increment. I am now weighing whether they will push the auction past $100.

If p2 drops at $99, I gain $1. If I drop at $98, they gain $2. Bidding $99 forces them to either pay $100 or lose the property.

I will bid $71. I am checking whether to mortgage Short Line before my next roll, since p2 is currently on that space.

I am on Water Works and will not roll immediately. The auction is on turn 92, so the next player may take over. I already own Reading and Pennsylvania Railroads that are mortgaged.

Unmortgaging railroads is too expensive. Three unmortgaged railroads would pay only $100 in rent, while the interest costs $100 to $200. I cannot afford that. I will bid $71 and mortgage Short Line immediately if I win. p2 may be trying to drain my cash, but I can outlast them to $99.
